## Overview

The Elasticsearch override of Birko.Data.EventSourcing's default event store ([[TASK-995]]). It is the default
`AsyncStoreEventStore` over the Elasticsearch store of `EventRecord`, plus an index refresh after every append. Obtained
without naming the backend: `factory.GetEventStore(o => o.AddElasticSearch())`.

## Key Design Decisions

**Why an override exists.** Every event store read is a search, and Elasticsearch shows a write to searches only after
the next refresh (by default each second). On the default store, the current version read 0 straight after an append, so
a writer that reloaded appended the same version again and conflicted with itself (measured at TASK-995: 5 of 9 contract
tests failed). After an append returns, every reader sees it.

**The refresh runs in `finally`**, so it also runs after a failed batch's compensation and the deleted events stop
showing. It is not cancellable, because the writes it makes visible have already happened. A failed refresh throws, and
says the events were written.

**Concurrency is the default store's.** A record's id is `EventRecord.IdFor(aggregate, version)`, and Elasticsearch's
create answers 409 for a taken id (`op_type=create`, TASK-625). Two clients racing on one version leave exactly one winner
(measured, TASK-995).

## Gotchas

- The index is `{IndexPrefix}_eventrecord`, like any Elasticsearch store's. It is created on first use, and the creation
  is safe when several clients start together ([[TASK-997]]).
- A batch is written one event at a time on Elasticsearch. A conflict deletes this batch's earlier events; a crash partway
  leaves them stored but invisible, and a later append clears them after the lease ([[TASK-1000]], in the default store).
  The store's checks of a batch are searches, so `MakeVisibleAsync` refreshes the index before them.
- Tests: `tests/Birko.Data.EventSourcing.ElasticSearch.Tests`, the shared contract, live under `BIRKO_ES_URL`.
